Chapter 16 · The economics

The Economics of AI Chips

Epoch AI estimated in December 2025 that Nvidia's B200 AI chip cost about $6,400 to build, mostly for memory and packaging. Its processor silicon cost about $900.

1,791 words / 8 min

Updated 3 October 2026·Cite this chapter·Report an error

Sharma, Yashvardhan. “The Economics of AI Chips.” Chip Supply Chain: How AI Chips Are Made. Updated 3 October 2026. https://chipsupplychain.org/component-costs/

In plain terms

A bill of materials is the list of parts inside a product and what each one costs to build. Epoch AI estimated in December 2025 that Nvidia's B200, an AI chip from its Blackwell line, cost about $6,400 to build[1]. The two logic dies, the pieces of silicon that do the calculating, cost about $900 of that[1]. The stacked memory beside them accounted for about half, and the packaging that wires the dies and memory together cost more than the dies[1]. Three firms, SK hynix, Samsung and Micron, dominate the world market for that memory[3]. One Taiwanese firm, TSMC, does that packaging[1].

In short

Reports in March 2024 put the B200's selling price at $30,000 to $40,000 per chip[1]. Epoch AI notes that most Blackwell revenue comes from servers and rack-scale systems, which may carry lower margins[1]. It says Nvidia's Blackwell margin may therefore be lower than the gap between cost and price suggests[1].

The estimate's memory price of $14 to $17 per gigabyte predates the 2026 rise in memory makers' sales and margins[5]. Micron's gross margin, the share of sales left after production costs, rose from 39.8 percent for the year to August 2025 to 86.8 percent in the quarter to September 2026[11]. Nvidia's was 75.0 percent in the quarter to July 2026[7].

Specimen · wafer cost

Epoch AI's December 2025 estimate of what it cost to build one B200, drawn as a column with each layer as tall as its share of the bill. From the bottom: $2,900 of memory in garnet, $1,100 of packaging, $1,000 of yield loss drawn hollow, $900 of logic dies, $480 of power delivery, board and test. The total is about $6,400, against a selling price of $30,000 to $40,000 per chip reported in March 2024.

See it in 3D in the interactive chapter

In December 2025 Epoch AI estimated that building one of Nvidia's Blackwell B200 chips cost about $6,400[1]. Reports in March 2024 put its selling price at $30,000 to $40,000 per chip[1]. Epoch AI's chip sales model, with data through October 2025, puts Nvidia's compute revenue per GPU in its GB200 rack systems at $33,000 to $42,000[2]. That figure leaves out the networking gear in those racks[2]. Some stages behind that $6,400 cost a lot because they are hard to make, some because capacity is short, and some because one firm sets the price.

How it works

Three numbers set the cost of a die, the finished rectangle of circuitry cut out of a wafer.

  • Wafer price. TSMC does not publish it. Nvidia makes Blackwell chips on a custom-built TSMC 4NP process[4]. Epoch AI estimates $17,000 for a 12-inch (300 mm) wafer on that process[1].
  • Dies per wafer. A wafer is a circle and dies are rectangles, so the edge of the wafer goes to waste. The bigger the die, the fewer fit. Each of the two logic dies in a B200 is about 800 mm2[1]. Nvidia calls them reticle-limited, meaning they are near the largest size a scanner can print in one shot[4].
  • Yield. Yield is the share of dies that work. Defects land at random, so a bigger die is more likely to catch one. Epoch AI models Blackwell die yield at 40 to 70 percent, centered on 60[1].

Together, those three numbers put the two dies inside a B200 at about $900[1]. The estimate counts only variable costs and leaves out fixed costs such as research and development[1].

Variants and trade-offs

Memory is the largest line

The largest line on the bill is the 192 GB of high-bandwidth memory beside those dies, a generation called HBM3E[1]. At $14 to $17 per gigabyte it comes to about $2,900, which Epoch AI counts as half of the build cost[1]. Epoch AI says HBM prices are negotiated deal by deal and can vary significantly with volume and contract length[1]. The $14 to $17 range dates from December 2025, before the 2026 rise in memory makers' sales and margins described below[5].

Three firms, SK hynix, Samsung and Micron, dominate the world market for that memory[3]. SK hynix says demand for its products has exceeded its available supply in recent quarters[6].

Packaging, substrate and test

CoWoS-L, the TSMC process that mounts dies and memory on one carrier and wires them together, adds about $1,100, more than the logic dies it carries[1]. Epoch AI models packaging yield at 65 to 95 percent[1]. A package that fails testing loses its logic dies and memory stacks[1]. Spreading that loss over the good units adds about $1,000 to each B200[1]. Power delivery hardware, the circuit board, and final assembly and testing add $480[1]. See Advanced packaging for why packaging capacity runs out first.

Epoch AI models each line as a range, deriving the packaging line from TSMC's advanced packaging revenue and Nvidia's share of CoWoS capacity[1]. The estimate covers the accelerator module only and leaves out servers and rack-scale systems[1]. Epoch AI notes that most Blackwell revenue comes from those systems, which may carry lower margins[1]. So, Epoch AI says, Nvidia's actual margin on Blackwell may be lower than the gap between this cost and the reported chip price suggests[1].

The B200 is used here because Epoch AI's line-by-line estimate covers it. In its results for the quarter to July 2026, Nvidia said its Vera Rubin platform was ramping into full production[7]. Each Rubin GPU carries up to 288 GB of HBM4, a newer generation of the stacked memory[8].

From package to rack to cluster

At rack scale, cost is measured per GPU-hour, one GPU running for one hour. For an operator that owns the machine, SemiAnalysis puts a Vera Rubin NVL72 at $3.57 per GPU-hour, against $1.84 for a GB200 and $2.36 for a GB300[9]. Each generation costs its owner more per hour than the last[9].

But SemiAnalysis finds Rubin cheaper per token than GB200 and GB300 at every interactivity level it compared[9]. A token is a short chunk of text, and interactivity is how many tokens per second each user receives. That finding rests on early results from the cloud provider CoreWeave running the DeepSeek R1 model, and SemiAnalysis has not verified them[9].

One level up, a cluster of 100,000 of Nvidia's earlier H100 GPUs costs over $4 billion in servers[10]. It needs more than 150 MW of data center capacity and uses 1.59 TWh a year, which costs $123.9 million at $0.078 per kWh[10]. In a rail-optimized network design, 98,304 optical transceivers link its GPUs to the first layer of switches, called leaf switches[10].

Who captures the value

ASE TechnologyPackaging and test segmentJune 202627.3%
AmkorOSATJune 202616.8%

Each figure comes from the firm's own earnings release[11][7][12][13][14][15][16][17][18][19]. The KLA and Ibiden releases give no percentage, so their figures are gross profit divided by revenue[13][17]. For ASE the table shows its packaging and test segment[18]. The company as a whole had a gross margin of 21.0 percent, because about a third of its revenue came from electronics manufacturing services, which earned 8.9 percent[18].

SK hynix's earnings release gives no gross margin. Its operating margin was 76 percent in the quarter to June 2026, and its revenue was up 257 percent from a year earlier[5].

In the table, design, equipment and leading-edge wafers earn gross margins of 50.3 to 75.0 percent, substrates 36.4 percent, and assembly and test 16.8 to 27.3 percent. In 2026 Micron passed all of them. Its gross margin rose from 39.8 percent for the year to August 2025 to 86.8 percent in the quarter to September 2026[11].

The Semiconductor Industry Association, using monthly data compiled by World Semiconductor Trade Statistics, counted $791.7 billion of global chip sales in 2025[20]. In its June 2026 forecast, World Semiconductor Trade Statistics put 2025 at $795.6 billion and 2026 at $1.51 trillion, with memory growing about 250 percent and logic 37 percent[21].

The industry group SEMI counted $135.1 billion of semiconductor equipment billings in 2025[22]. Capital spending at Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft and Oracle came to $448.2 billion in 2025, the sum of Epoch AI's quarterly figures[23]. Epoch AI says that spending would reach $770 billion in 2026 if the trend continues[23]. These totals overlap, so they cannot be added together.

Where the money goes

In Epoch AI's estimate for the B200, packaging and packaging yield loss together cost more than twice as much as the logic dies[1].

The table below sorts each stage by whether its cost falls as volume grows. The classes are a judgment drawn from the sources in this chapter and the stage chapters.

StageClassWhy
EUV lithographyStructurally expensiveOne supplier, ASML. See Lithography.
Masks and pelliclesStructurally expensiveEvery design needs its own mask set, and every EUV layer a flawless mask. See Photomasks and pellicles.
Metrology and inspectionStructurally expensiveKLA held about five times its nearest rival's share of these tools in 2025, by CSET's count. See Metrology and inspection.
HBMStructurally expensiveSK hynix says HBM needs more wafer input than ordinary DRAM. See Memory and HBM.
Advanced packaging, CoWoS-LStructurally expensiveModeled packaging yield is 65 to 95 percent, and a failed package loses its dies and memory.
ABF substratesStructurally expensiveInvestment can add substrate lines, but Ajinomoto said in June 2026 that the insulating film it makes for these substrates has held over 95 percent of its market since launch[24]. See Substrates and PCBs.
Power and cooling plantStructurally expensiveGrid connections face long queues, and GE Vernova's gas equipment backlog and slot reservations reached 116 GW in mid-2026. See Data centers and power.
Leading-edge logic wafersCompressible with scaleA very large die yields well only once a process matures. See Transistors and the front end.
Design and EDACompressible with scaleA design is paid for once, and its cost is spread across every chip sold. See Chip design, EDA and IP.
Deposition and etch toolsCompressible with scaleMost deposition and etch steps have three or four established tool makers. See Deposition and etch.
Optical transceiversCompressible with scaleNvidia agreed in March 2026 to invest $2 billion each in laser makers Coherent and Lumentum, with rights to future capacity. See Systems and networking.
Test and assembly (OSAT)Already commoditizedGross margins of 16.8 to 27.3 percent at Amkor and ASE's packaging and test segment, in the table above.
Wafers and bulk gasesAlready commoditizedSeveral firms make approved 300 mm wafers, and the top five served about 75 percent of the market in 2025. See Silicon and wafers.
Rack integration (ODM)Already commoditizedSeveral contract manufacturers on three continents assemble racks. See Systems and networking.

Review questions

Open a question to see its answer.

What does an Nvidia B200 cost to build, and what does it sell for?

About $6,400 to build, in Epoch AI's December 2025 estimate. Reports in March 2024 put its selling price at $30,000 to $40,000 per chip.

Nvidia's gross margin was 75.0 percent in the quarter to July 2026. Epoch AI notes that most revenue from Blackwell, the chip line that includes the B200, comes from servers and racks, which may carry lower margins. Reread: The B200 bill of materials

What is the most expensive part of an AI accelerator?

The stacked memory, about $2,900 in Epoch AI's December 2025 estimate, or about half of the cost to build.

The two logic chips that do the calculating cost about $900. Reread: Memory is the largest line

Why does packaging cost more than the logic chips?

A package that fails after assembly wastes the chips and the memory inside it.

In Epoch AI's estimate, packaging costs $1,100 and scrapped packages another $1,000, together more than twice the $900 for the logic chips. Reread: Packaging, substrate and test
